problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the limit given below?

$$
{lim}_{x\to (0,0)}\frac{xy-x{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+2xy}
$$

- The limit evaluates to $1$ along the path $y=x$
- The limit evaluates to $1$ along the path $y=-x$
- The limit exists and is equal to $1$
worked_solution:
Attempting to evaluate the limit by direct substitution leads to the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}:$

$$
{lim}_{x\to (0,0)}\frac{xy-x{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+2xy}=\frac{0\cdot 0-0\cdot {0}^{2}}{{0}^{2}+2\cdot 0\cdot 0}=\frac{0}{0}
$$

However, the function cannot be simplified by canceling common factors in the numerator and denominator:

We attempt to evaluate the limit by approaching $(0,0)$ from different paths.

- Statement I is false. Taking $x\to (0,0)$ along the path $y=x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (0,0)\,\,\,y=x}\frac{xy-x{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+2xy} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x(x)-x(x)^{2}}{{x}^{2}+2x(x)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}}{3{x}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{1-x}{3} \\  & =\frac{1-0}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is true. Taking $x\to (0,0)$ along the path $y=-x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (0,0)\,\,\,y=-x}\frac{xy-x{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+2xy} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x(-x)-x(-x)^{2}}{{x}^{2}+2x(-x)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{-{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}}{-{x}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}(1+x) \\  & =1+0 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is false. Because the limit evaluates to different results on two different paths, we conclude that the limit does not exist:

$$
{lim}_{x\to (0,0)}\frac{xy-x{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+2xy}=\text{DNE}
$$
